A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, complete 13-page versions of the same work. Corresponding sections, four result tables, Algorithm 1, equations and Appendix A proofs support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 report original VFM/G-VFM molecular-generation experiments, including continuous, joint and property-controlled generation results in Tables 2–4.

after.justification: v3 retains the original molecular-generation experiments and their reported outcomes, including end-to-end and Bayesian-inference conditional generation.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 changes the update base from x_{1,1} to x_{1,s}, the inner loop from 0…S to 0…S−1, and the velocity’s state index from t to k; it also drops the explicit predictor initialization. These revise the printed sampler, but unchanged Equation (15) leaves the intended implementation unclear. Objectives and architectures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate discrete generation on QM9/ZINC250k, continuous generation on QM9, joint generation on QM9/GEOM-Drugs, and QM9 conditioning on the same six molecular properties.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within every table, including Discrete FM in Table 1, EFM in Table 2, SemlaFlow in Table 3, and EDM, EQUIFM, GEOLDM and D-Flow in Table 4.

E3.justification: The reported experimental designs, metrics and model configurations are unchanged. Table 4 still evaluates MAE over 10K samples. The generic sampler edits do not establish a changed experimental protocol.

E4.justification: Both retain the brief Section 4.1 observation that atom and molecule stability fall below 80% without enforced equivariance. No ablations, robustness tests or supplementary empirical analyses are added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report point estimates without repeated-run or seed counts, uncertainty intervals, error bars or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–4 and narrative findings are unchanged. For example, G-VFM’s Table 2 NLL remains −120.7, and Table 4 polarizability MAEs remain 2.05, 2.25 and 1.98 for end-to-end, Bayesian inference and both, respectively.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, propositions, numbered equations and Appendix A.1–A.2 proofs are unchanged. The prose reference to Proposition 3.1 becomes 'Theorem 3.1', but its statement and proof are not revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about trained and post-hoc controlled generation, equivariance conditions, and performance across molecular-generation tasks.

C2.justification: The same interpretations and qualifications remain, including the proof-of-concept status of post-hoc inference, architectural comparisons with PONITA, and the tradeoff between D-Flow’s lower MAE and higher computational cost.

D1.justification: Architecture references, classifier-training guidance and other implementation/access information are retained. Although Algorithm 1 loses its initialization line, initialization at the predicted mean remains explicitly specified below Equation (15), so that technical information is still available.

R1.justification: v3 removes the Guzmán-Cordero et al. (2025) citation and bibliography entry for Exponential family variational flow matching for tabular data generation. The introduction correspondingly shortens its description of prior applications from general geometries and molecular generation to general geometries.

P1.justification: Edits are localized: an introduction sentence is shortened, Algorithm 1 changes from 'Sampling Controlled VFM' to 'Sampling Conditional VFM', and proof references change from 'Appendix' to 'Section'. Section organization and almost all prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 is reformatted with numbered lines and an 'Input' heading. Minor text and bibliography reflow occurs; the four result tables retain their structure and placement, and no figures are added or removed.

improvement.justification: Results, claims and proofs are unchanged. v3 clarifies some sampler indices but removes initialization from Algorithm 1 and changes its recurrence without reconciling it with the fixed-mean update in Equation (15). Because v2 already contained inconsistent pseudocode and initialization remains available in prose, these edits have an uncertain net effect on correctness and clarity.
